 JUDGMENT

The petitioners have filed this Petition under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act seeking Compensation of Rs.50,00,000/ for the Death of one Rakesh H.P. in a road traffic accident dated 02.02.2022.
2.

The case of the Petitioners' in brief is that:
SCCH-25 On 02.02.2022 at about 09.45am the deceased Mr. Rakesh H.P. being a pedestrian was crossing the T.B. Road, in front of Sanman Hotel very carefully,
cautiously observing the traffic rules and regulations.

At that moment, all of a sudden one Bolero Maxitruck bearing Reg.No.KA02AG1607 driven by its driver in a rash and negligent manner, endangering human life with high speed dashed against the deceased Rakesh H.P.
Due to impact, Rakesh H.P. sustained multiple fractures.

3. It is the further case of the petitioners that, immediately, he was shifted to nearest Srinivas Hospital wherein first aid was given and later he was shifted to NIMHANS for higher treatment wherein he took treatment for 15 days, multiple operations were done to Rakesh H.P. and after some days doctor advised his attendants for discharge and to admit and administer at local hospital at his native place.

Hence he was shifted to K.R. Pet Government hospital wherein he was admitted and treatments were continued as per the advice of SCCH-25 NIMHANS Doctors but he was declared as dead while taking treatment on 21.02.2022.

So far the petitioners have spent Rs.1,00,000/
towards treatment and another sum of Rs.50,000/ towards the transportation of dead body and another Rs.50,000/ towards the funeral expenses.
4.

It is the further case of the petitioners that, prior to the date of accident the deceased Rakesh H.P.
was hale and healthy, employed at Service Station at Bangalore, earning more than a sum of Rs.20,000/ per month.
Because of death of deceased Rakesh H.P., the petitioners have lost their bread earner of the family.
The accident was only due to the rash and negligent driving by the Driver of the said offending vehicle bearing No.KA02AG1607.

The jurisdictional police have registered a case and filed charge sheet against the driver of the said vehicle in Cr.No.21/2022 p/u/Sec.279,
338 and 304A of IPC.
The respondents being the insured and insurer of the said SCCH-25 offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the Petitioners.
Hence, this petition.
5. In response to the service of notice, the Respondents appeared through their respective counsels and filed separate written statements.

6. The objections of the Respondent No.1:

sentences.text: It has admitted the issuance of policy in respect of Respondent No.2 to the Maxi Truck bearing Reg.No.KA02AG 1607, it was in force as on the date of accident.

Further contended that the petitioners have lodged complaint against the insured vehicle by falsely implicating the vehicle and twisting the facts illegally and high handedly, colluding with the concerned persons in order to get compensation.
The driver of the offending vehicle did not have valid and effective DL as on the date of accident and the Respondent No.2 allowed such person to drive the same vehicle.
It has further contended that SCCH-25 there was no negligence on the part of the Driver of the insured vehicle.
It has submitted that the alleged accident occurred due to the sole negligence on the part of the deceased himself.
The police did not comply the terms and conditions u/Section 134  and 158(6) of M.V. Act.
It has denied the age, income, avocation, medical expenses etc., and contended that the compensation claimed by the petitioners is highly excessive and exorbitant.
Hence, prayed for dismissal of the petition.
7. The objections of the Respondent No.2:
This respondent admitted the ownership of the offending vehicle and contended that he has valid DL, FC, RC and permit as on the date of accident.
He has valid policy as on the date of accident.
Further, he denied the carelessness of the driver of the insured vehicle and contended that the accident occurred due to the deceased himself since he had the habit of driving alcohol .
He denied the accident, rashness of the driver of the offending SCCH-25 vehicle and the age, medical expenses, avocation and income of the petitioner.
Hence, prayed for dismissal of this petition.

8. On the above rival contentions of the parties, this court has framed the following issues:
1. Whether the Petitioners prove that, they are the legal heirs of the deceased Sri.
Rakesh H.P.?
2.

Whether the Petitioners prove that, Sri. Rakesh H.P., died on account of road traffic accident which took place on T.B.Road, infront of Sanman Hotel, due to rash and negligent driving by the driver of Bolero Maxitruck bearing Reg.No.KA02AG 1607, dated 02.02.2022 at about 9.45am?
3. Whether the Petitioners are entitled for compensation?
If so, how much and from whom payable 4.

What Order or Award?
9.
In order to prove their case, the Petitioners have examined Petitioner No.1 - Smt. Mangala -Mother of the deceased as PW.1 and got marked 16 documents as per Exs.P.1 SCCH-25 to P.16.
On the other side, the Respondents did not examine any witness nor produced any documents.

My finding to the above issues are as follows: Issue Nos.1 & 2 : In the affirmative Issue No.3 : In the affirmative, Issue No.4 : As per final order for the Following:
REASONS 12. Issue No.1:
It is the case of the Petitioners that, the Petitioner No.1 is the Mother, Petitioner No.2 is the Father and Petitioner No.3 is SCCH-25 the younger Brother of the deceased - Rakesh H.P.
The Petitioners to prove their relationship have examined the 1 st Petitioner as PW.1.
PW.1 has specifically spoken about this relationship in her chief examination.
Apart from that, to prove the relationship, the Petitioners have also produced Notarized copy of Aadhar card of the petitioner Nos.1 to 3 as per Ex.P.15.
In Ex.P.15  the Aadhar Cards of the Petitioners, the Petitioner No.1's husband's name and Petitioner No.3 father's name is mentioned as Puttegowda who is the petitioner No.2 in this case.
In Ex.P.7 - Inquest report of the deceased, his father's name is mentioned as Puttegowda.
These documents are public documents and they have got initial presumptive value under law.
These documents have not been seriously disputed by the Respondents.
The Respondents have not produced any contrary documents to dispute and rebut the contents of documents produced by the Petitioners.
As such, there are no reasons to discard the oral and documentary evidence produced by the SCCH-25 Petitioners.

Under such circumstances, relying upon the oral evidence of PW.1 and the documents, this court is of the opinion that the Petitioner No.1 is the mother, Petitioner No.2 is the father and petitioner No.3 is the younger brother of the deceased.
Accordingly, Issue No.1 is held in the affirmative.

13. Issue No.2:
The Petitioners to prove that the accident occurred due to the actionable negligence on the part of the driver of the offending Bolero Maxitruck have examined Petitioner No.1 as PW.1 and produced documents as per Exs.P.1, 2, 4 to 8, 11 and Mangala vs Tata Aig Gen Ins Co Ltd on 17 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/80888918/

sentences.text: PW.1 has reiterated the averments of the petition in her affidavit filed in lieu of her chief examination.
On the other hand, the Respondents Nos.1 & 2 have denied the involvement and negligence of the insured vehicle.

14. The documents produced by the Petitioners such as the FIR in Cr.No.21/2022 of Upparpet Traffic Police with FIS, SCCH-25 spot sketch, spot mahazar, MVA report, inquest report, PM report,
charge sheet and death certificate as per Exs.P.1, 2, 4 to 8 and P.11, 12 are all public documents and have initial presumptive value under law.
These documents fully and completely corroborate with the evidence of PW.1.

The investigation officer in crime No.21/2022 of Upparpet Traffic Police has conducted the investigation in detail and has filed the charge sheet against the driver of the Bolero Maxitruck bearing Reg. No.KA02AG1607 holding that the accident occurred due to the rash and negligent driving by the driver of the said vehicle.
During the cross examination of PW.1, she has stated that there is an under pass in majestic for pedestrians.
However, the Respondent No.1 has not obtained any contrary admission from the mouth of PW.1 to show the negligence of the deceased.

Therefore, there are no reasons to disbelieve the evidence of PW.1.
SCCH-25 15.

The Inquest report produced as per Ex.P.7 and PM report produced as per Ex.P.8 clearly shows that 'Death may be cardio respiration arrest post brain injury (vital organs)' following road traffic accident.
During the cross of PW.1 by the counsel for Respondent No.1, nothing worthwhile is elicited.
Ex.P.6 - MVA report shows that after testing Bolero Maxitruck motor vehicle on Road the brake system was in order and the brake of this motor vehicle is in good condition.
In support of their defence the respondents have not examined any witness nor produced any documents.
Therefore, I hold that the accident was caused due to the negligence of Bolero Maxitruck bearing Reg.No.KA02AG1607.
Accordingly, I answer Issue No.2 in the Affirmative.
16. Issue No. 3:
PW.1 has specifically spoken before this court that due to the untimely death of the deceased, they have lost the bread earner of their family and her loving son.

She has further SCCH-25 deposed that they have spent more than Rs.1,00,000/ towards treatment and another sum of Rs.50,000/ towards transportation of dead body and another Rs.50,000/ towards the funeral expenses.
Therefore, the Petitioners are entitled for compensation as per the following discussion.
Monthly income 17.
According to the Petitioners, the deceased was employed at Service Station at Bangalore and was earning a sum of Rs.20,000/ per month.
In this regard, the Petitioners have not produced any documents such as Bank statement, vouchers, etc., nor has she examined any witness.
Under such circumstances, this court has to consider the income of the deceased notionally for calculating the compensation.

sentences.text: .......The range of the wages between SCCH-25 highly skilled and unskilled labour may have to be considered by the Tribunal while assessing the income of the deceased........

However, such guidelines cannot take the place of statutory guidelines and therefore we hold that it would be proper to rely on the wages fixed under the Minimum Wages Act as a guideline and assess whether the deceased was a skilled or unskilled laborer".
19. It is pertinent to note that as per the Karnataka Government Notification of Minimum Wages for employment in Petrol Bunk, the monthly income of a supervisor is Rs.14,979/ per month.
The counsel for the petitioner has furnished the same Notification but the VDA is applicable from 01.04.2022.
However, the date of accident is 02.02..2022 and the older Notification has to be considered.
Therefore the notional income of the petitioner can be rounded off to Rs.15,000/ per month.
Age of the deceased 20.

In so far as age of the deceased is concerned, the Petitioners have produced true copy of PM report as per Ex.P.8.
SCCH-25
As per Ex.P.8 the deceased was aged about 23 years.
This is a public document and has got presumptive value under law.
This shows that as on the date of accident, the age of the deceased was 23 years.
Therefore, his age is considered as 23 years.
(i) LOSS OF DEPENDENCY AND FUTURE PROSPECTS:
As per the principles of law laid down in the case of Sarla Verma V/s Delhi Transport Corporation, appropriate multiplier applicable to his age is 18.

sentences.text:
In the instant case, the deceased has a Mother, father and younger brother, aged about 41,
42 and 20 years respectively.

PW.1 in her cross examination admitted that the petitioner No.2, her husband does not work anywhere, instead he takes care of the cattle at home and the petitioner No.3 is her second son and does coolie.
As such it can be considered that petitioner Nos.1 & 3 were not depending on the income of the deceased.
Therefore, petitioner SCCH-25 No.1 mother is considered as the dependent of the deceased.
However if the notional income is applied to the deceased, he would be earning around Rs.15,000/ per month.

sentences.text: As per the decision of Hon'ble Supreme court in National Insurance company Vs Pranay Sethi and others(AIR 2017 S.C 5157) persons aged about above 60 years are not entitled to any future prospects.

sentences.text: As mentioned above, since the deceased was under below 40 years age slab, 40% future prospects is to be added to his monthly income.

So Rs.6,000/ (Rs.15,000/ X 40% = Rs.6,000/)
should be added to his monthly salary of Rs.15,000/ then it comes to Rs.21,000/ per month.
As per the Sarala Verma case, if the deceased is a bachelor then 1/2 of his income has to be deducted towards his personal and living expenses, balance comes to Rs.10,500/.
Therefore, the total loss of dependency SCCH-25 would be Rs.22,68,000/ (Rs.10,500/ X 18 x 12) = Rs.22,68,000/).
(ii) LOSS OF CONSORTIUM:

In Magma General Insurance company Limited Vs. Nanuram (2018)
18 SCC 130, the Hon'ble Apex court has observed "Consortium" is a compendious term, which encompasses spousal consortium, parental consortium and filial consortium.

18 SCC 130
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The right to consortium would include the company, care, help, comfort, guidance, solace and affection of the deceased, which is a loss to his family.
With respect to a spouse, it would include sexual relations with the deceased spouse".
22. This observation of the Hon'ble Supreme Court is reaffirmed in United Indian Insurance Company Ltd. Vs. Satinder Kaur @ Satvinder Kaur and others, (2021) 11 SCC 780. SCCH-25 23.

sentences.text: The Petitioner No.1 is the mother and the petitioner Nos.2 and 3 are the Father and younger brother of the deceased.
The Mother, father and younger brother have to live remaining part of their life in the absence of their young son and elder brother.
The loss of a young son full of hopes for the future can never be suitably compensated to the parents.
However, petitioner Nos.1 to 3 are entitled to a sum of Rs.40,000/ each (Total Rs.1,20,000/) under the head of loss of consortium.
(iii) TRANSPORTATION AND FUNERAL EXPENSES AND LOSS OF ESTATE:

In so far as the funeral and transportation expenses are concerned, the Petitioners have contended that they have spent a sum of Rs.1,00,000/ towards transportation of dead body and funeral obsequies.

But,
there is no document produced in this regard.
The deceased was at K.R.Pet Government Hospital as per the advice of NIMHANS, he died during the treatment.
In SCCH-25 addition there are expenses during the death of a person for which documents cannot be maintained.
Therefore, in the interest of justice the Petitioners are awarded a sum of Rs.20,000/ under this head.
If the deceased was alive he would have certainly saved some amount out of his living and personal expenses and created an estate in favour of the Petitioners.

Therefore, the Petitioners are entitled for Rs.20,000/
under the head of loss of estate.
(iv) MEDICAL EXPENSES:
PW.1 has contended that they have spent Rs.1,00,000/ towards treatment.
In this regard they have produced 12 medical bills for a sum of Rs.9,891/.
There is no contrary evidence to these bills from the Respondents.
Therefore, Petitioners are entitled to the above said amount under this head.

sentences.text: Therefore, the Petitioners are entitled for a total sum of Rs.24,37,891/.
If it is rounded off it comes to Rs.24,38,000/ SCCH-25 Liability 24.
The Respondents have not proved their defence.
Therefore, the respondents being the insured and insurer of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioners.
The Petitioners have claimed an amount of Rs.50,00,000/, but they are entitled only for a sum of Rs.24,38,000/.
Therefore the Petition is liable to be allowed.
Accordingly I answer Issue No.3 in the affirmative.
25. Issue No.4:

In view of the findings of the above issue Nos.1 to 3, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
The Petition filed by the Petitioners under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act is hereby allowed with costs.

SCCH-25  The Petitioners are entitled for Compensation of Rs.24,38,000/ (Rupees Twenty Four Lakhs Thirty Eight Thousand only) along with interest at the rate of 6% p.a., from the date of Petition till the date of deposit of the Award amount and interest.
The Respondent Nos.1 & 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioners.
The respondent No.1 is liable to deposit compensation to the petitioners within 60 years from the date of suit till its realization.

On deposit of the award amount and interest, Rs.20,00,000/ shall be deposited in the name of the Petitioner No.1 in any N/S bank for a period of 3 years and Rs.40,000/ each shall be released to petitioner Nos.2 & 3 and the balance amount shall SCCH-25 be released to the petitioner No.1 by way of e payment with proper identification and due acknowledgment.
The Advocate's fee is fixed at Rs.1000/.
Draw Award accordingly.

Neeta and others Vs. Divisional Manager, MSRTC Kolhapur (2015)3 scc 590, Kala Devi and Orthers Vs. Bhagwan Das Chouhan and Others (2015) 2 SCC 771, Sonobanu Nazirbhai Mirza Vs.
Ahmadabad Municipal Transport Service (2013) 16 SCC 719, Pushkar Mehra Vs. Brij Mohan Kushwaha and others (2015) 12 SCC 688, Govind Yadav Vs. The New India Insurance Company Limited and another (2011) 10 SCC 683 and Ningamma and another Vs. United India Insurance Company Limited (2009) 13 SCC 710 has held that "there is a continuous and consistent trend by the Apex Court that the Minimum Wages Act provide for a source by which the notional income of the deceased, who had no valid proof of income could be assessed.
However, such guidelines cannot take the place of statutory guidelines and therefore we hold that it would be proper to rely on the wages fixed under the Minimum Wages Act as a guideline and assess whether the deceased was a skilled or unskilled laborer".
Therefore the notional income of the petitioner can be rounded off to Rs.15,000/ per month.
In so far as age of the deceased is concerned, the Petitioners have produced true copy of PM report as per Ex.P.8.

As per Ex.P.8 the deceased was aged about 23 years.
This is a public document and has got presumptive value under law.
This shows that as on the date of accident, the age of the deceased was 23 years.
Therefore, his age is considered as 23 years.
(i) LOSS OF DEPENDENCY AND FUTURE PROSPECTS:
As per the principles of law laid down in the case of Sarla Verma V/s Delhi Transport Corporation, appropriate multiplier applicable to his age is 18.
In the instant case, the deceased has a Mother, father and younger brother, aged about 41,
42 and 20 years respectively.
As such it can be considered that petitioner Nos.1 & 3 were not depending on the income of the deceased.
Therefore, petitioner SCCH-25 No.1 mother is considered as the dependent of the deceased.
However if the notional income is applied to the deceased, he would be earning around Rs.15,000/ per month.
